text: Given the upstream HighLevel API returns 429, When any tool calls it, Then the connector retries with backoff and, if still failing, returns the rate_limited error envelope rather than a raw passthrough
evidence: uv run pytest -v: both PASSED. test_client_retries_on_429_then_raises_rate_limited drives the real HighLevelClient._request retry loop against a fake httpx client returning 429 every time (asyncio.sleep patched out) and asserts exactly 4 attempts (1 + 3 retries) and 3 backoff sleeps before the rate_limited envelope surfaces.

text: Given two concurrent requests carrying two different sub-accounts' credentials (Location A and Location B), When both call highlevel_search_contacts at the same time, Then each response contains only its own Location's contacts
steps: Obtain two HighLevel sub-account (Location) Private Integration Tokens: A and B, each with at least one distinct contact not present in the other
Call POST /mcp tools/call highlevel_search_contacts with Location A's headers
Concurrently (or immediately after) call the same tool with Location B's headers
expect: Location A's response contains only Location A's contacts; Location B's response contains only Location B's contacts; neither list contains the other's contact
notes: needs two real HighLevel sub-accounts. Backend isolation mechanism (never reading a stale contextvar across concurrent requests) is covered by TC12, which passed.

text: Given valid credentials, When highlevel_create_contact is called with required fields and then highlevel_add_contact_note is called with the returned contact id, Then the note is visible when the contact is re-fetched

Call highlevel_add_contact_note with that contact_id and a note_text

text: Given a request's X-HighLevel-Location-Id header, When the connector builds its outbound call to the upstream API, Then the locationId used is always the one from that same request's context, never a value left over from a previous request
